label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Hi Mikaela, happy to give you the real version, you did so much for us when Dave did his shoulder, so it's the least I can do.

Short answer is we wouldn't go back. But here's the full picture.

We've got 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds, and we started on 21 Sept once mating was underway. We skip the arvo milking Tues, Thurs and Sat, plus Sunday arvo, so four once-a-days a week. Mornings are 5.15 every day.

Production is down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. The rep told us to expect 8-10, so we came in a bit better than that. Whether it's worth it depends on what the hours are worth to you, and for us they're worth a lot more than 6%.

Cells did go up, yes. We went from about 110k to around 180k in the first three weeks, which gave us a fright. It's back down to about 135k now, so not quite where it was but heading the right way. So no, they didn't go mental, but you will see them move and you need to be ready for that.

The bad bit I want you to know about: we had a heifer with mastitis that went bad on a skipped arvo. We didn't spot it until the next morning and she lost a quarter. That's on us really, but it's the risk. On the skip days you have to be right on your game with teat spraying and checking cows, because it bites you if you get lazy. Nobody's looking at them at the shed on those afternoons so you have to make a point of walking through them.

On the good side, lameness is way down. We've got 4 on the lame list now compared to 11 this time last year. We've got a long walk to the back paddocks (1.8km) so I think fewer trips up and down the race is making a real difference.

The cows got used to it quicker than I expected. About four days of bellowing at the gate and then they were fine. I was dreading it more than they minded it.

The best bit is the people side. Our first skipped Sunday arvo, Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday off in spring in 20 odd years! And Kieran, our 2IC, said it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October. Given you've got a young fella already talking about leaving, I'd take that seriously. And with Tom's knees, the arvos off will probably help him more than anything.

So I'm not going to talk you into it, because I don't want you blaming me in March, but we're glad we did it and we're sticking with it. If you do go ahead, I'd be putting a proper plan in place for checking cows and spraying on the skip days before you start.

Come and have a look at our shed rosters and numbers at the field day on the 19th if you like, I'll bring them along. Or just give me a ring if you'd rather talk it through, easier than me trying to type it all on my phone with my useless thumbs.

Bev
